title: Two ASASSN-14ko timing sets prefer different binary periods under constant intrinsic decay
abstract: We test whether a binary light-travel delay can hide constant intrinsic decay in the ASASSN-14ko event times from 2007 to 2026. We fit circular and eccentric Kepler delays, search period aliases, and map the circular fits to companion masses, velocities and orbit sizes. The main 21-event set prefers a circular period of 5.9 observer years with a 2.9-day light-time amplitude. Adding four early optical markers moves the fit to about 12 years and 6.7 days. Noise samples show broad and selection-dependent period ranges. Both circular fits require radial-velocity semi-amplitudes near 2500-2800 km/s. Thirty selection and jitter tests give best-fit amplitudes of 2231-2855 km/s. For an active black hole of 1e7 solar masses, the minimum companion masses are about 1.2e7 and 2.1e7 solar masses. Both circular solutions have room for the 108-day stellar orbit inside a basic Roche size scale. This does not prove three-body stability or a binary origin. The binary period is not secure, but the large velocity shifts give a direct test with flare-linked spectra. Results depend on constant marker lags, the quadratic intrinsic clock and bounded orbit searches. We provide code, source hashes, aggregate fits and conditional noise results.
